4.60.040. Fresno County Transportation Improvement Act Fund.

There is hereby established in the treasury of the County a special fund called the Fresno County
Transportation Improvement Act Fund, which shall be maintained by the County.

4.60.050. Receipt of Proceeds.

All revenue generated by this Act shall be deposited into the Fresno County Transportation
Improvement Act Fund.

A. Monies in the Fund shall be used to reimburse the County for the costs imposed by the
California Department of Tax and Fee Administration to collect and administer the tax imposed by

this Act, pursuant to Section 4.60.210.

B. The remaining monies in the Fund shall be appropriated each fiscal year to the Council of
Governments solely for the purposes specified in this Act.

4.60.070. Existing Neighborhood Streets and Roads Repair and Maintenance Program.

A. 1. Sixty-five percent of the annual revenue in the Fund shall be allocated for the purpose of
repairing, rebuilding, and maintaining the road system in the incorporated cities and the
unincorporated areas of the county region to improve travel time and accessibility, traffic safety, and
public health, as further provided in subsections B to H, inclusive.

2.a. The Council of Governments shall make separate allocations of funds under this section
to each of the incorporated cities within the county region, for expenditures by each city within its
own jurisdiction, and to the County, for expenditures in the unincorporated areas of the county

region.
b. Funds allocated under this paragraph 2 shall be distributed as follows:

i. Each jurisdiction shall receive a base allocation of four hundred thousand dollars
($400,000) each year.

ii. Following allocations made under clause i, the balance of funding to be allocated
under this section shall be allocated in proportion to each jurisdiction’s population based on the most
recent population estimates prepared by the California Department of Finance, weighted 80 percent,
and in proportion to each jurisdiction’s number of maintained public roadway miles as determined by
the most recent Pavement Condition Survey, weighted 20 percent. The allocation to the County shall
be based on the population and roadway miles in the unincorporated areas of the county region.

3. Each jurisdiction may use funds provided under this section for any program specified in
this section.

FRESNO COUNTY TRANSPORTATION IMPROVEMENT ACT MEASUKKE

The measure would impose one-half cent sales and use tax on taxable retail sales within Fresno
County for a period of 30 years. Based on estimated revenues comparable to the current Measure
C, the measure is expected to generate approximately $120 million in revenue during fiscal year
2027-28. Actual annual revenues may vary depending on taxable sales, economic conditions, and
other factors affecting sales and use tax collections.

The revenues generated by the measure would be dedicated to transportation-related purposes and
allocated pursuant to the measure. Based on estimated first-year revenues of $120 million,
approximately 65% ($78.0 million) would be allocated to Neighborhood Street Roads, 25% ($30.0
million) to Public Transportation, 4% ($4.8 million) to Regional Streets, 4% ($4.8 million) to

Access & Innovation, 1% ($1.2 million) to Airport purposes, and 1% ($1.2 million) to
Administration. A significant portion of the revenues would therefore be available for the
improvement, maintenance, rehabilitation, and other transportation-related needs of roads within

Fresno County.

The measure provides for Fresno Council of Governments (Fresno COG) to administer the
transportation program and associated funds. Accordingly, the County would not be responsible
for the administrative costs associated with administering the measure's transportation program,
except for any costs or responsibilities specifically assigned to the County under the measure or

applicable agreements.

If the measure is not approved, the proposed additional transportation sales tax revenues will not
be available. Transportation programs and projects currently supported by Measure C revenues
that are expected to continue under the proposed measure could, therefore, require alternative
sources of funding. Depending on the availability of other federal, state, local, and transportation
funding sources, additional County funding may be required to maintain or fund certain
transportation improvements, road projects, or services that otherwise would have been supported
by the measure's revenues. The amount of any additional County funding, if required, would
depend on future transportation needs, available funding sources, and decisions regarding the
prioritization and funding of transportation projects.

This measure would adopt the Fresno County Transportation Improvement Act, a County
of Fresno ordinance imposing a half-cent (0.5%) transactions and use tax (sales tax) for

2027, when the existing Measure C transportation tax expires, and would end thirty years
later unless extended by the voters. The California Department of Tax and Fee

Administration would administer and collect the tax.

Tax proceeds would be deposited into a County fund and appropriated to the Fresno
Council of Governments (COG), a joint powers agency governed by the fifteen
incorporated cities and the County. COG would annually allocate the proceeds as follows:

e 65% to the County and cities to repair, rebuild, and maintain local streets and
roads, including sidewalks, bicycle and pedestrian facilities, and safe routes to
school. Each jurisdiction would receive a $400,000 base allocation, with the
balance distributed by population (80%) and maintained roadway miles (20%). No
more than 5% of a jurisdiction’s allocation may be spent on road expansion, and
funds may not be used for streets in new growth areas.

e 25% to public transportation, with 10% to Clovis Transit, 70% to Fresno Area
Express, and 20% to Fresno County Rural Transit Agency.

e 1% to the Fresno Yosemite International Airport.

4% to regional street, road, and highway projects.

e 4% first to zero-fare transit for people with disabilities, veterans, seniors, children,
and students, then to competitive grants for clean energy and future transportation
technology projects.

e 1% to COG for administration.

Funds must supplement, not supplant, other transportation funding. Each jurisdiction
must extend the existing Regional Transportation Mitigation Fee agreement by June 30,

member Citizens Oversight Committee (Committee) appointed by the COG Policy Board

the COG Policy Board at least every ten years, conducted by the Committee, approved
by COG, and adopted by the Board of Supervisors if the amendments further the
purposes of the ordinance, with limited exceptions for declared emergencies and one-
time state or federal funding opportunities. Any change to the percentage allocations
among programs, and any other amendment, would require voter approval.
